extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners and attorneys practicing before the USPTO (and parties involved in USPTO disciplinary proceedings)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, statutory/regulatory requirements, and procedural expectations for practicing before the USPTO — covering fee payments, client-fund handling, communications with examiners, supervision, and OED disciplinary/remedial procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue fee payment timing (35 U.S.C. § 151)
rubrics_metrics.description: An issue fee must be paid in all allowed patent applications within three months of a written Notice of Allowance; if the issue fee is not timely paid, 'the application shall be regarded as abandoned.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO may accept a late payment and treat the application as though no abandonment occurred only if 'the delay in payment is shown to have been unavoidable.' Such a showing is made by filing a petition to revive under 37 C.F.R. § 1.137(a) together with the delayed issue fee payment and the fees required for filing the petition. Example from the page: Notice of Allowance stated issue fee 'MUST BE PAID WITHIN THREE MONTHS' (emphasis original); filing a transmittal after the deadline without a petition does not avoid abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment for failure to reply to Office action (35 U.S.C. § 133)
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to reply within the set or extended period for reply to an Office action 'will, by statute, cause the application to become ABANDONED (35 USC § 133).' The Office Action Summary sets the period for reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office actions commonly set a three-month shortened statutory period (with possible extensions); a reply may be filed late only within statutory extension rules and with appropriate extension requests/fees. Example: December 24 office action produced a deadline of three months from mailing date and in no event after six months from mailing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time to reply to Office actions (37 C.F.R. § 1.136(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions of time to reply may be available under 37 C.F.R. § 1.136(a); a late reply up to three months may be filed if accompanied by a request for an extension and payment of the appropriate fee(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reply after the shortened statutory period requires explicit extension request and fee; without proper extension and fees the application may become abandoned. Example: a late reply could have been filed up to June 24, 2009, if accompanied by a three-month extension request under § 1.136(a) and fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to revive abandoned application for unavoidable delay (37 C.F.R. § 1.137(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications abandoned for failure to pay the issue fee can be revived only if the delay in payment is shown to the satisfaction of the Director to have been unavoidable; such showing is made via a petition to revive under 37 C.F.R. § 1.137(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition to revive must be submitted with the delayed fee payment and the fees required for filing the petition. Filing a replacement payment without the petition and required fees is insufficient to revive an abandoned application under the 'unavoidable delay' standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing fee for dishonored checks (37 C.F.R. § 1.21(m))
rubrics_metrics.description: When a check submitted to the USPTO is dishonored, a processing fee under 37 C.F.R. § 1.21(m) is required (illustrated as $50.00 in the examples).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page examples repeatedly show $50.00 fees charged for processing dishonored checks (check numbers and dates cited). Ensure checks clear before relying on them for timely USPTO fee payments; dishonored-check fees add to amounts due.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of identity of client funds / prohibition on commingling (37 C.F.R. § 10.112)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must preserve the identity of client funds and property. Depositing client funds intended for USPTO fees into a business/operating account before paying the USPTO constitutes commingling and violates 37 C.F.R. § 10.112.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Respondent deposited client funds (government fee amounts) into his Sutton Operating Account and then paid with checks that were dishonored; the conduct is cited as commingling. Best practice: maintain separate client/trust or USPTO deposit accounts and do not mix client funds with business funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct adversely reflecting on fitness to practice (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct that adversely reflects on a practitioner's fitness to practice before the USPTO violates 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page cites submitting multiple checks drawn on insufficient funds as conduct that adversely reflects on fitness to practice (23 checks totaling $7,705.00). Such financial mismanagement and repeated dishonored payments are examples of the prohibited conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate preparation and supervision (37 C.F.R. § 10.77(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must not handle a legal matter without preparation adequate in the circumstances and must properly supervise subordinates. Failure to prepare adequately or to supervise subordinates can violate 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of inadequate supervision: an employee intentionally altered a USPTO document (erasing a mail date) that was then sent to a client; failure to timely pay an issue fee and failure to supervise employee drafting/filing documents were cited as violations. Remedial measures include monitoring subordinates and correcting deficiencies immediately, with follow-up monitoring for 60 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview summary requirement after examiner contact (37 C.F.R. § 1.133; MPEP § 713.04)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant or representative contacts a patent examiner (e.g., by telephone) to discuss a pending application, the result must be recorded in an 'Interview Summary' form which is entered in the application's official file (37 C.F.R. § 1.133; MPEP § 713.04).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page notes no Interview Summary was present for the alleged pre-abandonment contact; examiners' recollections and file entries are expected. Failure to prepare and file an interview summary when required undermines the official record and may be scrutinized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office action mail date and mailing cover page (MPEP § 707 and related practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Office actions include a PTOL-90A mail cover page with a 'Mail Date' field, and the Office Action Summary specifies the period for reply; practitioners should rely on the official mail date and the indicated reply period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page shows the office action had 'Mail Date' = '12/24/2008' on PTOL-90A and the Office Action Summary stated the reply period. An altered copy sent to a client that removed the mail date can cause confusion regarding due dates. Best practice: preserve and transmit complete Office action documents (including mail date fields) to clients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of certificate of mailing on fee transmittal
rubrics_metrics.description: A transmittal form may include a certificate of mailing date which indicates mailing and can be relevant to establishing dates (e.g., Issue Fee Transmittal Form included a certificate of mailing dated Feb 20, 2007).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While certificate of mailing is evidence of mailing date, a timely payment must still actually clear per statutory deadlines; a certificate alone does not substitute for the statutory three‑month payment requirement if the check is dishonored and the fee is not received within the statutory period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedial auditing and client remediation requirements after discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: If client matters may have been compromised, the respondent must hire a Qualified Third Party to conduct an independent audit of affected files, file a written report summarizing the audit, and take reasonable steps to remedy adverse consequences identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specified timeframes in the Final Order: hire a Qualified Third Party within 30 days; file the audit report within seven months; within eight months take all reasonable steps to remedy adverse consequences and inform OED Director in writing with corroborating documentation. Example: audit to ensure clients' rights have not been adversely affected by altered/fraudulent documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to affected clients/assignees and counseling
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must prepare and send a letter to the owner/assignee of an affected patent advising of the facts (including issue-fee-related facts) and must send verification of receipt to the OED Director within prescribed timeframes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example required content: explanation of issue-fee deadlines and events (Notice of Allowance, transmittal, dishonored check, abandonment, replacement payment without petition). The letter must be sent by certified mail and verification provided to OED within 30 days from Final Order signature in the example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opening and maintaining a USPTO deposit account and deposit-account instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: A remedial/administrative measure: open a USPTO Deposit Account and maintain a minimum balance (example: $1,000), and include a specific deposit-account instruction paragraph in correspondence when fees are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example instruction to include in correspondence: 'Please charge any additional amounts that may be due in connection with this filing to Deposit Account 504246. Please credit any excess fees to such deposit account.' This is a best practice to avoid dishonored checks and commingling issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary notice, publication, and reporting obligations (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.59, 11.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: OED will publish Final Orders and Notices of Stayed Suspension, and pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 the OED Director will give notice of public discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies where respondent is admitted and to courts where admitted. Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.20(a)(4), the respondent must provide copies of the Final Order to state bars and identified individuals and file an affidavit of compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication venues include the OED Reading Room and the Official Gazette. Respondent must provide copies of the Final Order within specified days (example: within thirty days to state bars) and file an affidavit within a specified period (example: forty-five days) confirming compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order to Show Cause and potential lifting of stayed suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director believes the respondent failed to comply with the Final Order or disciplinary rules during the stayed period, the Director shall issue an Order to Show Cause why the stay should not be lifted and the respondent suspended (procedural steps specified).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure example: Order to Show Cause is sent to respondent's last address of record; respondent has fifteen days to respond; after consideration, OED Director may deliver the Order to Show Cause, response, and evidence to the USPTO Director and request lifting the stay and suspension for up to 36 months. This describes enforcement mechanics for non‑compliance with remedial terms.
